_comment: Issue #1084 half A. The states this consumer must tell apart, plus the refusal semantics it inherits from skillc's verified-result contract - including the FORGED verdict, which is well formed and only re-derivation can catch.
limits: WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES: that the CONSUMER renders a recorded failure as a failure, a recorded pass as a pass, an absent artifact as neither, and an envelope it cannot read as a refusal rather than a guess. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT OF #1084: anything at all about a behavioural case discriminating. There is no behavioural case - half B lives in skillc and waits on skillc #8, #9 and #10. Every case here is a FIXTURE written by hand to exercise a reading, and the gate says so on every verdict it prints, because its output sits in `make verify` beside gates whose greens carry behavioural meaning and a reader skimming cannot tell them apart. A green here is evidence about a reader, never about a model. THE ABSENT CASE IS THE REPOSITORY'S ACTUAL STATE: nothing produces one of these artifacts today, so the real gate reports `absent` on every run until half B lands. That is why `absent` is a DETECTION rather than a pass - an unknowable answer is never rendered as a clean one (#1014, #800) - and why it is not a build failure either, which is the Makefile's consumption decision rather than this gate's verdict. THE FORGED PAIR IS WHY THIS GATE DERIVES RATHER THAN READS: `bad-forged-pass-violation` and `bad-forged-pass-no-mandatory` both declare status PASS, both are well-formed JSON, and both parse - their own criteria derive FAIL and INCONCLUSIVE respectively. A consumer that trusted the declared status would launder each as a clean pass, and no amount of validating the record's SHAPE would catch either. The second is this repository's #1014 rule ('an unknowable answer is never rendered as a clean one') arriving inside someone else's record format: records.md fixes that no mandatory criteria yields INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS. THREE CASES CAME FROM COUNTER-MODEL REVIEW AND ARE THE ONES A SINGLE AUTHOR WOULD NOT HAVE WRITTEN: `bad-malformed-mandatory-flag` carries `"mandatory": "true"` as a STRING, which the derivation read as falsy and silently dropped the VIOLATED criterion out of the population - the record then derived PASS honestly, matched its declared PASS, and reported clean, so no assertion about agreement between status and criteria could have caught it. `bad-wrong-kind` is an `artifact-manifest` read as a verified-result. `bad-unhashable-status` carries `"status": []`, which JSON permits and `in frozenset(...)` raises TypeError on - the traceback exited 1, this gate's `failure` code, printing no verdict line at all, and the advisory `|| true` wrappers swallowed it. All three are WELL-FORMED JSON and all three previously produced a confident wrong answer rather than noise. VERSION 2 (skillc PR #32): every case is a version-2 record, because skillc now refuses version 1 and this gate reading only v1 would have refused the first real record skillc could emit. `bad-version-one` is the old good case VERBATIM - the regression pin that a v1 record is now refused, not read. Five cases are skillc's own v2 RECORD rules restated here: `bad-version-boolean`, `bad-producer-subject` (the forged subject verdict, reported `forged`), `bad-satisfied-without-evidence` (would otherwise derive PASS), `bad-no-graded-digests`. TWO CASES ARE REAL GRADER OUTPUT, not hand-written: `good-skillc-graded-pass` and `bad-skillc-graded-failure` wrap skillc 3c243a1's `grade_slug.py` report on its reference candidate and on `wrong/example-only`, so the consumer is tested against what the producer's grader actually emits rather than against this author's reading of the spec. Every verdict is 'checked alone - NOT against any ledger': skillc's bundle rules are not applied here.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the gate is new, so there is no previous blind version to vendor. This is 'check the behavioural eval produced valid output' written directly - parse each artifact, complain if one is malformed, otherwise report clean - which is what someone writes when the artifact is thought of as OUTPUT TO BE VALIDATED rather than as a VERDICT TO BE READ. skillc's contract names this exact framing as the thing that must not be trusted: 'A valid JSON record, hash or echoed config alone does not authenticate success.' It is blind three ways at once - it never reads `status`, so a recorded FAIL reads clean; it has nothing to validate when no artifact exists, so ABSENT reads clean; and it never reads `version`, so an envelope it cannot understand reads clean. It AGREES with the real gate on a genuine PASS, which is what makes the three misses load-bearing rather than evidence the anchor is merely broken. It is blind to the FORGED pair for the same root reason and most sharply: both are well-formed and parse, so a framing built on 'validate the output' cannot distinguish them however carefully it is written - only re-deriving status from criteria can. It is equally blind to the three counter-model cases: all are valid JSON, so 'validate the output' parses each without complaint and reports clean.
